purpose.summary: This is a patient cost-sharing (patient co-payment) calculation subroutine for inpatient billing, part of the JMA ORCA standard medical receipt software used in Japanese medical institutions. It computes patient burden amounts (負担金算定) for various insurance combinations including national health insurance, public assistance, and regional subsidies. It handles complex Japanese medical insurance rules including income-based limits, long-term hospitalization, and multiple public subsidy schemes.

notable_features: No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS — pure COBOL logic
No COMP-3 usage despite being a financial calculation program
87 CALL statements indicating heavy use of external subroutines
294 PERFORM statements reflecting complex calculation logic
Large working storage with many calculation work areas (WK-KEISAN, WK-TOKUSYU, etc.)
OCCURS clauses for multi-insurance (up to 4 public subsidies)
Japanese-language comments encoded in EUC-JP or Shift-JIS (rendered as latin-1 artifacts)
Extensive revision history spanning 2002-2005 with 80+ documented changes
Part of the open-source JMA ORCA project (Japan Medical Association)
verdict.notes: The file is 602KB / 12071 lines — a very large production subprogram. Japanese comments are encoded in a multi-byte encoding (likely EUC-JP) but were decoded as latin-1, causing mojibake in the displayed text. The program is clearly part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system. No COMP-3 is unusual for financial COBOL but consistent with some GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL coding styles. Source was truncated to 16000 chars; the full procedure division was not visible but structural indicators confirm all four divisions are present.
